title: DSpark: confidence-scheduled speculative decoding with semi-autoregressive generation
gist: A drafter that proposes a block of tokens at once, with a confidence head predicting how many will survive checking. A scheduler then admits draft tokens per request until a profiled throughput curve stops improving, so the amount of speculation grows at moderate load and shrinks as concurrency rises.
changes: Speculative decoding that listens to the load, in production at a model lab. It is the clearest case of two levers being tuned together: how far to speculate is set by how full the batches are.
caveats: Self-reported; offline numbers were measured with the scheduler switched off, and the paper warns its strict-latency figures are not typical. An open-engine reproduction confirmed the trend, not the numbers. Drafting cost is wasted on requests where little is accepted.

numbers.metric: Aggregate throughput at moderate latency targets, live traffic

bears_on.note: Acceptance differs by domain and the best amount of speculation changes with load, so the setting cannot be fixed.
The adaptation is per request and per load level, done by one scheduler for everyone, not built per customer.
